twitter.lead: News that learns what you like

linkedin.title: I started building a news app when I was a teenager because I was tired of missing the stories that actually mattered to me.
linkedin.body:
It felt like the news landscape was broken. We were either bombarded with sensational headlines meant to trigger a reaction or buried under an endless stream of noise that felt disconnected from my life. I wanted something that respected my time and my intelligence.

Building Headlinne wasn't about trying to disrupt the industry or chasing the latest hype cycle. It was about solving a personal problem. I wanted a way to filter out the noise and find the signal. I wanted technology that worked for me, not against my attention span.

We built this using AI, not because AI is popular, but because it is the only way to genuinely personalize the experience at scale. It allows us to learn what you care about and deliver news that actually fits your interests. It is about making information useful again rather than just abundant.

The journey has taught me that the best products often come from the simplest frustrations. We are still learning and iterating every single day, but the goal remains the same: to make staying informed feel like a privilege instead of a chore.
linkedin.cta: If you are ready to rethink how you consume your daily news, you can try it yourself at HEADLINNE.com.

story_card.headline: OpenAI PR shuts down questions on user suicide
story_card.standfirst: A publicist interrupted an interview when the CEO was asked about a tragic user incident.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: OpenAI's PR team tried to stop a journalist from asking CEO Sam Altman about a user's suicide.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Vanity Fair editor Mark Guiducci brought up the incident during an interview with Altman.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: It raises questions about how much control companies keep over interviews regarding safety.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Look for how OpenAI handles future inquiries about their platform's safety and impact.

story_card.caption:
OpenAI publicist tried to stop Sam Altman interview over questions about a ChatGPT user suicide.

During a profile interview, the editor questioned the CEO about a user who died by suicide. The PR representative immediately tried to change the subject, citing time constraints. This interaction highlights the tension between tech companies managing their public image and the serious safety concerns surrounding their tools.
